first_installment_sketch: The model-optionality experiment: two workers, Nemotron and Laguna, completed one mission and independent verification passed. Killing Laguna mid-mission did not kill the mission. The brain kept the meaning; the hand was swapped. Model identity is execution metadata, not mission meaning, which is exactly why the router stays deterministic: task type, capabilities, data class, context, tools, latency, and verification select the worker, never model reputation.
hook: We killed the model mid-mission. The mission did not notice.
thesis: ONE BRAIN, MANY HANDS is a recurring franchise: runtime optionality with authority staying put. Each installment demonstrates a hand being swapped while the brain's authority, identity, and evidence semantics remain untouched. The standing seam doctrine: every seam must buy replaceability, and external execution state is evidence, never PING truth.
